Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates: Find here all the live updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 28th September 2026.

The Sensex plunged 1,124.02 points, or 1.52 per cent, to settle at 72,771.72 on Monday, while the Nifty 50 shed 360.25 points, or 1.56 per cent, to close at 22,780.25.

Among Nifty 50 components, Dr Reddy’s Laboratories, Infosys and HDFC Life managed to close in the green. TMPV, Adani Enterprises, Jio Financial and Power Grid were among the major laggards.

No major index was spared in Monday’s sell-off, with the Nifty PSU Bank index emerging as the worst performer, falling 3.24 per cent. The Nifty SmallCap 100 plunged 1.85 per cent, while the Nifty MidCap 100 crashed 1.63 per cent.

The rupee depreciated 28 paise to close at 96.03 (provisional) against the US dollar on Monday, on risk-off sentiments in global markets after the US rejected a deal proposal by Iran, diminishing hopes of reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

MIT-WPU School of Commerce & Economics signing an MoU with FPSB India to enable eligible students to pursue the CFP® certification pathway alongside their academic programmes.

The collaboration aims to strengthen financial planning and wealth management education, while equipping students with globally benchmarked knowledge and career-ready skills for the evolving financial services sector.

The release also highlights the growing demand for qualified financial planning professionals in India and the opportunities emerging across banking, investment advisory, wealth management, insurance and fintech.

Trilegal advised on the initial public offering by National Stock Exchange of India Limited (“NSE”) of 126,436,650 equity shares, aggregating to ₹225.62 billion. The offering marks the largest initial public offering (“IPO”) in India year-to-date and the second largest IPO in India to date. NSE is also the largest stock exchange in India.

The IPO comprised a pure offer for sale by existing shareholders. NSE had a shareholder base of over 200,000 shareholders, who were provided an opportunity to participate as selling shareholders in the offer for sale.

Trilegal advised certain shareholders in connection with the IPO.

The IPO was managed by a syndicate of 19 book running lead managers.

The Trilegal Capital Markets team advising on the transaction was led by Partners: Richa Choudhary and Maitreya Rajurkar; and comprised Senior Associate: Sanya Chaudhari; and Associate: Siddhant Mishra.

PSP businesses of both companies to be merged into Saarathi, a 100% subsidiary of QMS

The merged entity would aim at capturing leadership position amidst complementary capabilities across enrolment, adherence, camps, distribution and patient engagement

Mumbai, September 28, 2026: Health Care At Home India Pvt Ltd (HCAH) and QMS Medical Allied Services Limited (QMS) (NSE: QMSMEDI), a leading integrated healthcare solutions company listed on the NSE Main Board, today announced the signing of definitive documents for a strategic merger of their pharma services businesses to create a scaled provider of patient support program (PSP) solutions for pharmaceutical companies across India. Under the terms, the PSP business verticals of both HCAH and QMS would merge into Saarathi Healthcare, a 100% subsidiary of QMS.

Together, the combined platform will operate 160+ Patient Support Programs impacting over 1.2 million+ patients, supported by 2,000+ professionals across 35+ cities, with complementary capabilities spanning patient screening, enrolment, therapy initiation, adherence, patient assistance and disease management. The combined entity will be India’s largest patient support platform, serving top Indian and MNC pharma companies. The partnership is intended to create a larger and more comprehensive platform while maintaining continuity for existing clients, programs and teams through the transition.

Mahesh Makhija, Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, QMS Medical Allied Services Limited, said: “The combination brings together two complementary platforms with strong capabilities across patient support and engagement. By bringing these capabilities together, we aim to create greater scale, reach and execution capability for pharmaceutical companies while helping more patients access the support they need throughout their treatment journey. This initiative would also fortify the value creation for the shareholders at QMS.”

Bank of India has gone live with User-Level Programmable CBDC and Auto Issuance on its Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) platform, built by Montran India, the companies announced today. Built in line with Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) guidelines, the capability was formally announced in Mumbai.

The feature lets a user schedule automatic issuance of digital rupee (e₹) to a beneficiary’s CBDC wallet, at a set amount and frequency, while defining the purpose the funds can be used for. Instead of authorizing the same transfer by hand every month, the sender configures it once. The system handles the recurrence, and the funds carry their intended use with them.
